clue.text: In resort, both made to buy a popular song

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a new order, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday resort where two people are pushed into buying something popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In resort' reads as being at a seaside town, but split as re-sort it is the anagram signal for 'both made to buy a'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Noël Coward number, a hit standard, so it is an example of a popular song.

clue.text: Film famous racehorse keeling over — extremely unpleasant

indicators.note: keeling over means falling over, so the horse's name is turned backwards

parts.note: Red Rum won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s
most foul means as nasty as can be

explanation.surface: A celebrated horse collapsing is a dreadful sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is a legendary British racehorse; 'keeling over' turns REDRUM round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1964 Miss Marple movie starring Margaret Rutherford.

clue.text: Fault of French and Italian blocking me on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letters sit on top of the river letter
the Italian letters sit at the foot of the column, blocking its bottom

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and an Italian blocking someone's way along a river is unfortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone, a failing or flaw.

clue.text: Give evidence from stand, then watch

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate
to witness something is to watch it happen

explanation.surface: Testifying from the witness box, then observing the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify to something under oath is the idiom for giving evidence.

clue.text: America supporting centre for refugees along with African country

indicators.note: in a down clue the America letter supports the rest from below
centre for means the middle two letters of refugees are taken

parts.note: and means along with

explanation.surface: The United States backing a refugee centre in an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a landlocked East African nation, so it is an example of a country in Africa.

clue.text: Wicked and frightening

definitions.meaning: wicked in slang means excellent or great
in its original sense the word means causing terror

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the modern sense is marvellous, the older sense is terror-inducing.

clue.text: Age of English artist

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: How old an English painter is.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a long historical period, an epoch.

clue.text: Cricket side, ahead of test, being judged

indicators.note: ahead of says the cricket letters come before the test letters

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A cricket team is assessed before a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, or leg side, is the half of the field behind the batter's legs; a Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone facing a court case is being tried, so they are being judged.

clue.text: In good time outlaw must receive justice, at great cost

indicators.note: must receive says the justice word is taken inside the outlaw word

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban
right means justice
dearly means at a high price

explanation.surface: A criminal must face justice, however high the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something early in the morning and promptly is the idiom for being punctual and in good time.

clue.text: Cake produced by graduate following dance

indicators.note: the graduate's letters come after the dance's letters, following them

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A cake baked by someone fresh from university who has just been dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-soaked yeast sponge, a classic French-style dessert, so it is a kind of cake.

clue.text: See 26
Nobleman briefly getting attention

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat being given notice after a quick word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend or give someone your ear is to pay heed to them, so the word stands for attention.

clue.text: We make a call about going on without a band

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the word for going on

parts.note: adding is going on, as in carrying on with more remarks
to ring is to make a phone call

explanation.surface: Someone phoning to complain about a musical group playing on without its full line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group, but it is the definition, a ring worn on the finger; 'without' drops A from ADDING, leaving DDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gold hoop placed on the finger at a marriage ceremony is a band in the jewellery sense.

clue.text: New and reportedly coarser shopkeeper

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for coarser is heard, not spelt

parts.note: grosser means coarser or more vulgar

explanation.surface: A rough new trader behind the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of fruit and vegetables is a kind of shop owner.

clue.text: Greek character, say, heading off to change

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for say is removed

parts.note: to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: A Greek person, perhaps, leaving in order to make a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes S from STATE, leaving TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form, a direct synonym of change in its infinitive sense.

clue.text: Place in the schedule: male in draw lost out

indicators.note: in says the male letter goes inside the word for draw

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

indicators.note: out means the letters of lost are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who lost in a drawn match gets a slot on the fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is an allotted period in a broadcasting or appointment timetable.

clue.text: First-rate attic here?

definitions.meaning: first-rate means of the highest standard
an attic is found on the uppermost storey of a house

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, an attic being literally on the highest floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest rank means first-rate, and the uppermost floor of a building is where an attic sits.

clue.text: Remained steady at sea in operation

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of steady are mixed up

parts.note: a machine that is on is in operation

explanation.surface: A ship kept steady while sailing on some mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To have remained somewhere beyond the expected time is the phrasal verb meaning stuck around.

clue.text: Porter collecting mail for messenger

indicators.note: collecting says the word for porter gathers the mail word inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
post is mail

explanation.surface: A hotel porter picking up the letters for a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman, but here it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is literally one sent out, a messenger who spreads a teaching.

clue.text: Virginia and I occupying tavern to no avail

indicators.note: occupying says the letters for Virginia and I sit inside the word for tavern

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Two people take over a pub, but it comes to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without success or result is futile, an idiom meaning without any useful outcome.

clue.text: A permit received by the runner

indicators.note: received by says the permit word goes inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A licence given to someone who runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is a sportsperson who competes in track events, an example of that kind of competitor.

clue.text: One inside provides for addicts

indicators.note: inside says the letter for one sits within the other word

parts.note: to fend for someone is to provide for them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone inside supplies drug users.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can mean an enthusiast or addict, as in a dope fiend.

clue.text: Infantryman pays for veteran heading for reunion

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it, so foots means pays
an oldie is an old-timer, a veteran

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of reunion is taken

explanation.surface: A former serviceman covers the costs of a regimental get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who fights on foot, as opposed to cavalry, is a member of the infantry.

clue.text: Gardening tool to sharpen, not new

indicators.note: not says the letter for new is left out

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: A garden implement that needs sharpening because it is old.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled blade for weeding and loosening soil is a common gardening implement.

clue.text: Actor and raconteur, Justin, overbearing in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer and storyteller named Justin who is domineering in his role.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ustinov was a celebrated British actor, writer and famously witty teller of anecdotes.

clue.text: Name old hospital drama

explanation.surface: Naming an old hospital in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is classical Japanese masked theatre, a traditional form of drama.

clue.text: Pile taken from cart our cleaner used

indicators.note: used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A heap of rubbish removed from a cart by a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a heap, but it is an old name for the device, from the first atomic pile.
explanation.definitionFit: The first fission reactors were stacked graphite blocks called atomic piles, so pile is an older term for one.

clue.text: Laparoscopy essential — her role Guy's set out

parts.note: key means essential or crucial

indicators.note: set out means the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A medic's vital part in an operation at Guy's, a London teaching hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's is a major London hospital, which fits the medical surface; 'set out' rearranges HER ROLE GUYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laparoscopy is abdominal investigation through tiny incisions with a camera, the classic minimally invasive operation.
